abstract: This document is a short laboratory procedure for an acid-base titration. It instructs the student to calibrate a burette with deionized water, pipette 25.0 mL of unknown HCl into a clean Erlenmeyer flask, and add three drops of phenolphthalein indicator. The unknown is then titrated with standardized NaOH until the first persistent pink color appears, the NaOH volume is recorded, and the process is repeated for two more trials and averaged.
headline: Step-by-step acid-base titration procedure for determining the concentration of unknown HCl using standardized NaOH and phenolphthalein…
key_points: The procedure begins by calibrating the burette with deionized water.
A 25.0 mL sample of unknown HCl is pipetted into a clean Erlenmeyer flask.
Three drops of phenolphthalein are added as the indicator before titration.
Standardized NaOH is added slowly until the first persistent pink color appears.
The volume of NaOH used is recorded for each trial.
Two additional trials are performed and the results are averaged.
